A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GC-xLSTM work and provide readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–F. The relocated checklist, reordered appendices, and renumbered results can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v2 reports original GC-xLSTM evaluations on Lorenz-96, fMRI simulations, and VAR, alongside learned weather, motion, and financial graphs and training/scaling analyses.

after.justification: v5 retains these original results and adds a component ablation on Lorenz-96 and fMRI in Table 3.

M1.justification: Section 4 revises the reported forecasting procedure from predicting H=10 future steps, or H=5 for VAR, to next-step prediction with optimization at each time step. The sparse projection, sLSTM backbone, adaptive losses, and Algorithm 1 otherwise remain unchanged.

E1.justification: The same six dataset families and GC discovery tasks remain, including the same motion activities. The new ablation reuses Lorenz-96 and fMRI. Table 5 labels fMRI as real-world, but Appendix C still explicitly describes simulations; this does not establish different data coverage.

E2.justification: The comparator sets in the existing Lorenz-96 and fMRI benchmark tables are unchanged. The new ablation in v5 Table 3 adds two evaluated controls: LSTM with the joint optimizer, and xLSTM with standard Group Lasso.

E3.justification: Besides the revised forecast horizon, v5 reports company-data context C=40 instead of the previously stated C=10. Appendix C changes its feature count from 20 to 19, consistent with the already 19-variable Figure 7. The ablation introduces controlled component substitutions. These reported revisions do not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v5 adds the first controlled ablation isolating both central design choices: the xLSTM forecaster and joint sparsity optimization. Table 3 evaluates their replacements on Lorenz-96 F=40 and fMRI, substantially expanding evidence about what drives performance. Existing lag-specific, training-dynamics, and scaling analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report standard deviations, as specified in checklist item 7; the new ablation follows that practice. Neither specifies experimental repeat counts or seeds, and no uncertainty-estimation or significance-testing procedure changes. Table 5's sample counts describe datasets, not repeated runs.

E6.justification: v5 Table 3 adds balanced accuracies of 93.0±0.3 and 62.8±2.0 for LSTM with joint optimization on Lorenz-96 and fMRI, respectively, and 73.0±4.6 and 65.4±2.0 for xLSTM with Group Lasso. Existing benchmark values and empirical graphical results are retained; v2's VAR Table 3 becomes v5 Table 4.

T1.justification: Section 2 newly assumes strictly stationary time series. The GC definition, loss and gradient derivations, complexity analysis, and Appendix B approximation argument remain substantively unchanged. The added expressivity citation does not supply a new proof.

C1.justification: v5 removes v2's separate contribution claiming that the training regime increases the underlying model's robustness and reduces noise sensitivity. The main claims about GC-xLSTM, adaptive strict sparsity, and robust discovery across simulated and real-world applications remain.

C2.justification: v5 interprets the ablation as evidence for both architectural capacity and joint optimization. Appendix D newly cautions that only some relationships in the full financial graph are economically plausible, qualifying the favorable discussion of its selected excerpt. The existing limitations concerning proofs and scaling remain.

D1.justification: Table 5 newly documents motion-recording lengths and sample counts and consolidates dataset settings. Appendix C discloses brief simulation burn-in periods, and Section 4 explicitly identifies baseline scores as taken from their original papers. The code-access pointer changes from an anonymous mirror to a named GitHub repository.

R1.justification: v5 adds Auer et al. on expressivity and Pettenuzzo and White, Das and Babadi, and Rubenstein et al. when connecting Granger and Pearlian causality. It also adds a brief comparison with state-space models. Divo and Kraus publication updates refer to existing cited works.

P1.justification: v5 makes localized language and author/header edits, reformats the contributions, reorders model-analysis paragraphs, moves the checklist before the appendices, and swaps Appendices E/F. Most prose remains recognizable. Some precise algorithm-line references deteriorate into erroneous wording such as 'algorithms 1 to 1.'

P2.justification: v5 adds the ablation and dataset-summary tables, adds a Year column to Table 1, revises Figure 2 and several captions, and resizes or relocates existing displays. The training and scaling figures exchange numbering and position while retaining their plotted content. The overall page format remains unchanged.

improvement.justification: The ablation supplies previously missing evidence for both central components, while additional settings and the financial-graph qualification improve transparency. These gains outweigh limited regressions: Table 5 inconsistently labels simulated fMRI as real-world and attributes VAR to the Lorenz-96 reference, and algorithm-line references are broken. The retained main results and theoretical support make this a limited overall improvement.
